title: Configuration
text:
Copy the template and replace its CHANGE_ME values:
There is no default configuration path. Pass --config before the command, or set it once for the current shell:
To use an encrypted configuration, encrypt it with SOPS and enable decryption with either --sops or RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1:
The values of id fields are user-defined names. They only need to be unique within their section; references in other sections must match them exactly. Every item may also have an optional description for user notes. Descriptions do not affect backup behavior.

title: Configuration
text:
credentials
credentials contains reusable S3 authentication details. Backblaze application key IDs and application keys use the same fields as AWS access keys.
credentials:
  - id: b2-credentials
    description: Backblaze B2 application credentials.
    access-key-id: "..."
    secret-access-key: "..."
One credential may be referenced by several stores.

title: Configuration
text:
restic-stores
restic-stores describes each restic repository and links it to an entry in credentials through credentials-id.
restic-stores:
  - id: b2-store
    description: Backblaze B2 restic repository.
    credentials-id: b2-credentials
    enabled: true
    endpoint: https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
    region: us-west-004
    bucket: example-bucket
    key_prefix: voice-memos
    password: "..."
All stores use restic’s S3 backend. endpoint identifies the S3-compatible service, region configures request signing, and bucket plus key_prefix locate the repository. password encrypts the restic repository. Disabled stores are ignored by commands and may retain CHANGE_ME placeholders. An enabled store fails validation until its store values and credentials are complete.
Every store appears in the generic list repository table. generic init initializes enabled stores even when no backup references them; a backup entry is required before using that store with generic backup or generic run.

title: Configuration
text:
backups
backups defines the entries shown in the CLI’s Backups table. Each entry selects a repository by matching restic-store-id to a restic-stores.id value.
backups:
  - id: documents
    description: Back up local documents.
    restic-store-id: b2-store
    paths:
      - ~/Documents
      - ~/Desktop
    # Optional; defaults to the backup ID.
    # tag: documents
id is the stable name used to select the configured backup in commands and menus. paths is the non-empty list of local files or directories passed to restic backup; ~ is expanded to the current user’s home directory. Relative paths remain relative to the directory where the command is run.
tag is optional restic metadata applied automatically to every snapshot created through that backup. It defaults to id, so it normally does not need to be configured. Restic generates a unique snapshot ID after each successful backup; a snapshot ID is not a configuration value.
Run the configured backup with:
uv run restic-backups generic backup documents
Restic scans the configured paths and creates a new snapshot. It stores only new or changed file data, while the snapshot still represents the complete state of those paths at that time.
Several backups may share a restic store. Their tags distinguish their snapshots inside the shared repository.
Specialized workflows may discover their own sources and omit paths. For example, the voice-memos subcommand locates the macOS recording store itself. generic backup reports an error if the selected backup has no configured paths.

title: Configuration
text:
Optional archive policy
AWS stores may add an archive policy. storage-class controls how new objects are stored, and restore defines retrieval behavior for cold storage:
credentials:
  - id: aws-credentials
    description: AWS S3 access credentials.
    access-key-id: "..."
    secret-access-key: "..."

restic-stores:
  - id: aws-store
    description: AWS S3 restic repository.
    credentials-id: aws-credentials
    enabled: false
    endpoint: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
    region: us-east-1
    bucket: example-bucket
    key_prefix: backups
    password: "..."
    archive:
      storage-class: GLACIER_IR
      restore: null
Omit archive to use the storage provider’s default class.
Use GLACIER_IR for immediate restic access. It must not define a restore policy:
archive:
  storage-class: GLACIER_IR
  restore: null
Cold classes require an explicit retrieval policy:
archive:
  storage-class: GLACIER
  restore:
    tier: Bulk
    days: 7
    timeout: 24h
GLACIER accepts Standard, Bulk, or Expedited; DEEP_ARCHIVE accepts Standard or Bulk. Retrieval commands also require an acknowledgement:
ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1 uv run restic-backups generic run \
  --backup <backup-id> restore latest --target <dir>
Changing a storage class affects new objects only. Use a new key_prefix rather than mixing storage policies in one repository.

title: Configuration
text:
Validation rules
check-config also rejects duplicate IDs, unknown credential or store references, missing S3 fields, empty or invalid paths, and invalid Glacier retrieval tiers or durations. Managed-data resolution separately rejects unsafe path components.

title: Quick Start
text: This guide creates one generic S3-compatible backup from a source checkout.

title: Quick Start
text:
1. Install
make install-deps
make install
make install-deps installs the required Homebrew tools. make install creates the uv environment.

title: Quick Start
Quick Start
text:
3. Initialize and back up
Initialize a new repository once:
uv run restic-backups generic init
Then create a snapshot from the paths configured for documents:
uv run restic-backups generic backup documents
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents snapshots
Running generic init again is safe: existing repositories are detected and skipped. Initialization covers every enabled repository; generic backup uses the selected backup’s repository, paths, and default or configured tag.

title: Quick Start
text:
4. Verify a restore
mkdir -p /tmp/restic-restore-check
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents \
  restore latest --target /tmp/restic-restore-check
Inspect the restored files before relying on the backup. Continue with Generic Backups for repository commands or Voice Memos Backups for the macOS workflow.






Warning



Do not commit config.yaml, credentials, repository passwords, or restored data. Use SOPS configuration before committing a config.

title: Generic Backups
text:
The generic subcommand runs standard restic operations against any configured backup. Backup sources may be files or directories anywhere on the machine.
Set RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG first, or pass --config before generic. See the Quick Start for a complete first backup.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Commands








Command
Purpose
Remote storage




generic list
Show repository and backup tables
No


generic data-dir [BACKUP]
Print the managed private-data directory
No


generic init
Initialize each new enabled repository
Yes


generic backup [BACKUP]
Create a snapshot from configured paths
Yes


generic forget [BACKUP]
Forget one tagged snapshot and prune
Yes


generic destroy [REPOSITORY]
Permanently erase one repository
Yes


generic run --backup ID ...
Pass trailing arguments directly to restic
Depends on restic command



backup, data-dir, and run prompt for a backup when it is omitted in an interactive terminal. Non-interactive callers must provide the backup ID.
Running restic-backups generic without a subcommand in an interactive terminal opens a command menu. Explicit subcommands remain available for scripts and scheduled jobs. Run a restic command reads the installed restic version’s command list and descriptions, lets you select one, then prompts only for its arguments. Enter --help at that prompt to see the selected command’s options.
generic list has separate Repositories and Backups tables, so enabled stores remain visible even when no configured backup references them.
generic init reports each configured store, skips disabled or already initialized stores, and initializes every enabled store that is missing.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Create a snapshot
Configure the local source paths once, then select the backup by its ID:
backups:
  - id: documents
    restic-store-id: personal-store
    paths:
      - ~/Documents
      - ~/Desktop
uv run restic-backups generic backup documents
The command expands ~, passes the paths to restic backup, and applies the backup ID as the restic tag unless tag is explicitly configured. Every run creates a snapshot of the complete source state while restic uploads only new or changed file data.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Forget one snapshot
uv run restic-backups generic forget
Forgetting is interactive-only. Select a configured backup, select one snapshot with its configured restic tag, and confirm. The CLI runs restic forget --prune, so the snapshot and data no longer referenced by any other snapshot are permanently removed. The configured backup and repository remain available.
When several configured backups share a repository, their restic tags keep their snapshots distinct in the picker.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Permanently destroy a repository
uv run restic-backups generic destroy
Destruction is interactive-only. The CLI shows the full S3 target, asks for a yes/no confirmation, then requires the exact repository ID. It deletes every object, object version, and delete marker below the configured bucket and key_prefix. It does not delete the bucket or change the YAML configuration.
The provider credentials need permission to list objects and versions and to delete objects and versions. An empty key_prefix is always rejected to prevent accidental bucket deletion.

Repository deletion is irreversible. Snapshots, indexes, repository keys, and encrypted data are all erased. The configured restic password cannot recover them.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Common operations
# Inspect and check the repository
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents snapshots --tag documents
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents check

# Restore a snapshot
uv run restic-backups generic run --backup documents \
  restore <snapshot-id> --target /tmp/documents-restore
Arguments after the backup selection are passed to restic unchanged. The CLI exports the selected repository and credentials only to the child process and does not print them. For the backup command, it also adds the configured restic tag automatically; additional --tag arguments remain supported.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Managed data directory
uv run restic-backups generic data-dir documents
The result follows data/<store-id>/<bucket>/<key-prefix>/<backup-id>/ beside the selected config file. It is for private generated metadata; generic backup sources do not need to live there.

title: Generic Backups
text:
Cold S3 storage
GLACIER_IR supports immediate access. GLACIER and DEEP_ARCHIVE permit uploads, but retrieval-related commands require the configured restore policy and an explicit acknowledgement:
ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1 uv run restic-backups generic run \
  --backup archive restore latest --target /tmp/archive-restore
Other restic commands are rejected for cold repositories when the CLI cannot determine that they are safe. See Configuration for the archive policy fields.

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
The voice-memos command backs up the macOS recording store and produces private JSON transcripts, summaries, tags, indexes, and speaker diarization. There is no separate Voice Memos Makefile.
Set RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG first; set RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1 too when the file is SOPS-encrypted. See Configuration.

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Requirements

Give the terminal Full Disk Access.
Open Voice Memos and wait for iCloud synchronization.
Run LM Studio at http://localhost:1234/v1 when producing summaries.
Set HF_TOKEN for speaker diarization.

The default recording source is:
~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.VoiceMemos.shared/Recordings

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Safe routine
uv run restic-backups voice-memos status
uv run restic-backups voice-memos backup
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe
uv run restic-backups voice-memos backup
uv run restic-backups voice-memos check
uv run restic-backups voice-memos restore latest --target /tmp/voice-memos-restore
The second backup captures newly generated summaries. Verify a restore before deleting recordings from any device; iCloud synchronization is not a backup.

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Commands







Command
Purpose




backup
Back up recordings and summaries together


snapshots
List repository snapshots


check
Verify repository structure and metadata


stats
Show latest tagged snapshot size and file count


files [SNAPSHOT]
List files in a snapshot


restore [SNAPSHOT] --target DIR
Restore a snapshot


get UUID [--restore]
Resolve a summary to its recording and reveal it


transcribe
Incrementally transcribe and summarise


status
Count processed, pending, stale, and errored memos


diarize
Add speakers to existing transcript segments


diarize-parallel
Split pending diarization across worker processes


dashboard [LOG_DIR]
Watch parallel worker progress


diarize-status
Count transcripts with and without speakers


migrate-layout
Move flat JSON records into monthly directories


prune-index
Remove index entries whose JSON is missing


rebuild-index
Rebuild the index from JSON records on disk


peek
Inspect the Voice Memos database schema



Run uv run restic-backups voice-memos COMMAND --help for exact options.

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Transcription variants
# Incremental transcription and summaries
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe

# Reprocess all memos or selected UUIDs
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe --all
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe --uuids ABC-123,DEF-456

# Reuse transcripts for new summaries, or omit summaries entirely
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe --summary-only --all
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe --no-summary

# Force retranscription
uv run restic-backups voice-memos transcribe --all --no-summary --force
The available engines are whisper-mlx and whisper-mlx-turbo.

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Parallel diarization
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...
uv run restic-backups voice-memos diarize-parallel --workers 3 --dashboard
Workers write logs beneath a temporary diarize-chunks-* directory. Use --detach to leave them running without the dashboard, then attach with:
uv run restic-backups voice-memos dashboard

title: Voice Memos Backups
text:
Generated data
The CLI derives the summary directory from the configured voice-memos backup:
uv run restic-backups generic data-dir voice-memos
All generated JSON and indexes remain beneath that ignored private directory.

title: Restic Backups
text: Restic Backups is a YAML configuration and CLI layer for multiple restic repositories, with optional SOPS decryption. It supports reusable S3-compatible credentials, multiple buckets and key prefixes, managed private metadata directories, and a complete macOS Voice Memos workflow.

title: Restic Backups
text:
Start here

Quick Start creates, validates, and restores a first backup.
Configuration describes credentials, stores, backups, and Glacier policy.
Generic Backups covers standard restic operations for any local files or directories.
Voice Memos Backups covers backup, transcription, recovery, and diarization on macOS.

title: Restic Backups
text:
Architecture
restic_backups/
  cli.py                 root command wiring and global options
  config.py              YAML loading and validation
  generic/
    cli.py               generic restic command definitions
    sops.py              SOPS decryption
    repository.py        repository resolution and managed paths
    restic.py            restic execution and archive policy
    s3.py                permanent repository destruction
  voice_memos/
    cli.py               Voice Memos command definitions
    pipeline.py          transcription and diarization processing
    workflow.py          backup, restore, and recording lookup
    parallel.py          worker process orchestration
    dashboard.py         live Textual dashboard
Command modules contain command definitions and option handling. Config, SOPS, repository, pipeline, workflow, and parallel modules perform the operational work.

title: Restic Backups
text:
Private data boundary
Managed artifacts use:
data/<store-id>/<bucket>/<key-prefix>/<backup-id>/
This path is relative to the selected configuration file. It does not constrain backup sources; commands may pass absolute source paths outside the repository. Everything below data/ is ignored.






Warning



Commit config.sops.yaml only while encrypted. Never commit credentials, recordings, transcripts, summaries, caches, restores, or restic data.

title: CLI
text:
Run the installed command through uv:
Commands that use a repository require a configuration file. Pass the global options before the command:
The equivalent environment variables are RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG and RESTIC_BACKUPS_SOPS=1. See Configuration for setup.
Commands use colored, level-aware stderr logging for configuration and operation progress. Add --verbose before the command, or set RESTIC_BACKUPS_VERBOSE=1, to include command-level details without printing credentials or repository passwords:

title: CLI
text:
Root commands








Command
Purpose
Remote storage




check-config
Load and validate configuration
No


generic ...
Run generic configured repository commands
Depends on subcommand


voice-memos ...
Run the macOS Voice Memos workflow
Depends on subcommand



Use Generic Backups for restic passthrough, repository initialization, restores, and managed data directories. Use Voice Memos Backups for the macOS-specific workflow.
Run subcommand help without loading a configuration:
uv run restic-backups generic --help
uv run restic-backups voice-memos --help
